paper.title: Wealth condensation in a simple model of economy

headline: Bouchaud-Mézard 2000 (agent-based mean-field): 3/3 locked clauses REPRO; Gini mu=1.4/2/3/5 = 0.66/0.50/0.37/0.27; mu=2 tail slope=-1.89, max/mean=47, Hill mu-hat=1.78

verdicts.gate: P1 inequality decreases monotonically with redistribution J: Gini(mu=2)∈[.45,.55], (mu=3)∈[.33,.42], (mu=5)∈[.22,.32], strict decrease mu=1.4>2>3>5
P2 stationary tail is a genuine POWER LAW at mu=2: CCDF top-decile slope∈[-2.5,-1.5], 99.9pct/mean>=12, max/mean>=25, power-law beats exponential by AIC
P3 tail exponent mu-hat tracks mu=1+J/sigma^2 in ordering: Hill mu-hat at mu=2 ∈[1.5,2.6] AND mu-hat monotone increasing over the J-sweep

extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic mean-field model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce the redistribution-tunable Pareto wealth condensation (multiplicative growth => power-law tail, distinct from a conserved-exchange exponential) and would catch an artifact

citations: Bouchaud, J.-P. & Mézard, M. (2000). Wealth condensation in a simple model of economy. Physica A 282:536-545. doi:10.1016/S0378-4371(00)00205-3.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded against the stationary Gini bands, the heavy-tail ratios + CCDF slope + Hill exponent, and a power-law-vs-exponential AIC on the top decile
